summary: Unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS: the Compress middleware pins ~18 MiB of zstd encoder state per in-flight response
description:
## Summary

There is a potential vulnerability in Traefik's Compress middleware. When `zstd` is one of the enabled encodings (the default), the middleware creates its zstd encoder with the library default options, which hold about 18 MiB of memory for each response until the response is fully written. An unauthenticated client that opens many concurrent requests and reads the responses slowly can make Traefik hold an unbounded amount of memory and crash. The patched versions bound the encoder memory to less than 1 MiB per response, with no change to the compressed output.

Traefik v2 is not affected: zstd support in the Compress middleware was introduced in v3.1.0. The end-of-life v3 lines from v3.1 to v3.6 are affected and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched version.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.18
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0-rc.2

## For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please [open an issue](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues).

cwes.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

summary: Incomplete fix for GHSA-hrpp-p4fc-wwf8 allows ForwardAuth NTLM authentication bypass via Proxy-Authorization
description:
## Summary

There is a high severity authentication vulnerability in Traefik's ForwardAuth middleware when the authentication server uses a connection-bound scheme such as NTLM or SPNEGO/Kerberos "Negotiate". The fix for GHSA-hrpp-p4fc-wwf8 sends the subrequests of a client that presents such a credential on a dedicated connection to the authentication server, but it only detects the credential in the `Authorization` header. ForwardAuth also forwards the `Proxy-Authorization` header, and a credential sent in that header still goes through the connection pool shared by every client. An unauthenticated client can then reuse an authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity through `authResponseHeaders`, and access the backend as that user. The patched versions apply the same isolation to `Proxy-Authorization`.

Traefik v3.0 through v3.6 are end-of-life and are also affected; they will not receive a fix on their own line. As a workaround, set `authRequestHeaders` to a list that does not include `Proxy-Authorization`.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.62
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.18
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0-rc.2

## For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please [open an issue](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues).
